AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 16, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a)
  – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Michael F G Trust; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Daniel Heraldez
  New Harvest Church Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Natalia Padilla
  ASB Vice President, St. Linus School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim November 27, 2021 as Small Business Saturday in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim November 2021 as Native American Heritage Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Presentation by Jeffrey Prang, Los Angeles Tax Assessor.

  3.  Halloween Recap.

  4.  Veterans Day Recap.
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  November 2, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 3, 2021 –
  October 16, 2021, in the total amount of $926,915.28. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 28, 2021 – November 10, 2021, in the total amount of $4,397,672.02. 640

  Report

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Juan Manuel
  Anguiano. 830-01

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 21-1729 - GRANTING A NON-PUBLIC UTILITY PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO
  HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Ordinance No. 21-1729, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK GRANTING A PIPELINE
  FRANCHISE TO HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED. 618-16

  Report

  7.  AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT ANNUAL SHORT RANGE TRANSIT PLAN FOR FISCAL YEARS 2022-
  2024 - Staff recommends City Council receive and file the Triennial Short Range Transit Plan, and
  authorize the Executive Director of Regional Transportation to submit the updated Short Range Transit
  Plan to Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority. 1130

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-68 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – PROJECT NO. 7438R1 - ADVANCED
  METERING INFRASTRUCTURE METER SYSTEM INSTALLATION PHASE 2 – Staff recommends
  City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-68, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE WATER ENTERPRISE FUNDS TO PROJECT NO.
  7438R1 – ADVANCED METERING INFRASTRUCTURE (AMI) METER SYSTEM INSTALLATION
  PHASE 2, in the amount of $223,144; and

  b.  award a construction contract to Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc. for Project No. 7438R1,
  Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) Meter System Installation Phase 2, in the amount of
  $566,410; and authorize the City Manager to execute the contract, and any amendments, provided
  there is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the
   City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610/1005-04-7438

  Report

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 21-70 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD FORMER NORWALK REDEVELOPMENT
  AGENCY’S BOND PROCEEDS AND AMENDMENT NO. 1 – ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
  SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-70, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD FUNDING FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT CONTRACT SERVICES, in the
  amount of $55,000; and

  b.  approve Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with Kosmont Companies to provide economic
  development services in an amount not to exceed $87,960; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment and any further amendments provided there is funding in the budget and
  it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 325/610

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 21-71 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE HOUSING
  ASSET FUNDS FOR CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT COMPLIANCE SERVICES
  AND APPROVE AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE ON-CALL BUILDING AND PLANNING
  CONSULTING SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-71, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT COMPLIANCE SERVICES FOR THE
  CALIFORNIA YOUTH AUTHORITY PROPERTY, PROJECT NO. 7859; in the amount of $359,755;
  and

  b.  approve Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with Michael Baker International, Inc. dated January
  25, 2021, to provide California Environmental Quality Act Compliance Services for the California
  Youth Authority property, City Project No. 7859, in an amount not to exceed $359,755; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 1 and any additional amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610/940-01/1405-02

  Report

REPORTS

  12. JANUARY 2022 MEETING SCHEDULE – Staff recommends City Council either:

  a.  direct staff to take the appropriate steps to move the meetings to January 11 and 25, 2022; or

  b.  cancel the January 4, 2022 meeting and authorize holding one regularly scheduled meeting on
  January 18, 2022. 825

  Report

  13. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 4 – AGREEMENT FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT / HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIP PROGRAM PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AND
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT CORONAVIRUS RESPONSE FUNDS AND
  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 – PROFESSIONAL SERVICES FOR PLANNING AND
  ADMINISTRATION OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT CARES ACT FUNDS / HOME-
  AMERICAN RECOVERY PLAN FUNDS – Staff recommends City Council approve:

  a.  Amendment No. 4 to the agreement with Michael Baker International, Inc. dated July 1, 2019 to
  provide on-call Community Development Block Grant and HOME Investment Partnership
  Programs professional services in an amount not to exceed $68,540; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment and any additional amendments not-to-exceed $100,000
   provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney; and

  b.  Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with Michael Baker International, Inc. dated May 19, 2020 to
  provide on-call CDBG professional services in an amount not to exceed $365,941; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the amendment and any additional amendments not-to-exceed
  $100,000 provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 315

  Report

  14. PARK PROJECTS UPDATE - GRANT FUNDING REQUEST, NORWALK PARK MASTER PLAN, AND
  CLOSURE OF SKATE PARK - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  approve the use of Proposition 68 per capita funds to proceed with improvements at Bob White
  Park; and authorize the City Manager to execute the funding application and required documents,
  on behalf of the City; in a form approved by the City Attorney;

  b.  approve the closure of Norwalk Skate Park and removal of equipment. 920-03/10/14/17

  Report

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 21-69 - APPROVING EMPLOYEES’ PREMIUM PAY USING AMERICAN RESCUE
  PLAN ACT’S STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 21-69, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING EMPLOYEES’ PREMIUM PAY USING AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT’S STATE AND
  LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS.

  Report

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated November 10, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
